One dawn, as the sun bled over the horizon, Aro cast his handmade net woven from sea grass and wishes into the stillness. The ocean sighed, a deep, resonant sound that rippled across the Salt Teeth.

From the depths, fish of every color and shape sprang forth, wriggling into being as if awakened from a long slumber. Aro, stunned by the bounty spilling from the deep, knew then that he must give back. He whispered a pledge to the waves, forever binding his fate to the sea, promising to protect its hidden heart. The fisherman was a legend in his own time, and his deeds were told and retold by fishermen and sailors alike. But he was also a feared figure, for his powers were said to be dangerous and unpredictable.

One day, the fisherman decided to sail into the unknown, to explore the world beyond the Salt Teeth. He took with him a small boat and a single fishing rod, and he set out into the great sea.

He sailed for many days, and many nights, and he saw many strange and wonderful things. He saw islands of crystal, and forests of fire, and mountains of ice.

C. In those days, a man came to the island of Cascais, and he had a boat and a net, and he cast his net to fish. He was there for many days and many nights, and he caught many fish, and he ate and he was well.
But one day, he caught a fish that was the biggest he had ever seen, and he could not pull it in. It pulled him into the sea, and he could not let go. He held on for days and days, and he saw the fish swim down deep, deep into the sea.
On the fifth day, the man saw a light shining in the depths of the sea. He could see it was a woman, and she was beautiful. She reached out her hand, and she pulled the man out of the water. He was safe, and he was alive.
The woman said to him, "You have saved me. I am the queen of the sea. I will give you a gift. You will never want for food again."
And with that, she disappeared into the depths of the sea.
